story.conflict: I blamed everything else first: the model, the vector DB, the client data. $40K in hosted API bills across two quarters while our swarm retried failed tool calls in loops nobody logged. A Rajkot retail pilot with 1,140 leads exposed it — 38-minute median response, 3.4% qualification, because Sheets queued every lead and email notified after the buyer had joined three rival chats. The board kept asking about traffic. The failure was the missing ledger: no tenant_id, no latency_ms, no policy_decision on any call. Without that, every retry was invisible spend.
story.hook: It was 11:40pm in Junagadh when my swarm billed $217 in one night and delivered nothing. Four agents, all green in the notebook, all dead in prod — one hallucinated a Postgres schema, one retried a timed-out tool 19 times, and the client demo was in 9 hours. I sat with the JSONL log and counted the damage line by line.
story.payoff: The fix took 9 days on a Rs 6K per month VPS: typed Pydantic tool schemas with strict bounds, Open Policy Agent tenant isolation on every call, and a human checkpoint before any payment or invoice mutation. Median form-to-WhatsApp link fell from 38 minutes to 87 seconds, qualification rose 4.8x to 16.4%, and 41 payments cleared Rs 1,16,850 by day 22. The swarm was not broken. The guardrails were missing. We stopped chaining prompts and started gating every state change — and the same traffic finally paid.
